subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A 'storyboard' is most useful for planning...
options: A sequence such as an animation or advert
questions.explain: A storyboard sketches a sequence of frames to plan how an animation or film will unfold.

questions.q: 'Installation art' is best described as...
options: A small painting hung on a wall
A three-dimensional work that transforms a whole space for the viewer to enter
questions.explain: Installation art creates an immersive environment, often filling a space the viewer moves through.

questions.q: Red is often chosen in branding to suggest...
questions.explain: Red carries strong associations of energy, excitement and urgency, useful for grabbing attention.

questions.q: What is a 'contact sheet' used for in photography?
options: Viewing many small thumbnail images to select the best shots
questions.explain: A contact sheet shows small versions of all the frames so the photographer can choose which to develop.

questions.q: Cubism is most associated with which two artists?
questions.explain: Cubism was pioneered by Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque in the early 20th century.

questions.q: In a repeating textile print, the single unit that repeats is called the...
questions.explain: The motif is the design unit that is repeated across the fabric to form an all-over pattern.

questions.q: A 'wordmark' (logotype) is a logo made from...
options: A stylised version of the brand's name in text
questions.explain: A wordmark is a logo formed from the company name set in distinctive, designed lettering.

questions.q: In 3D work, 'armature' refers to...
options: An internal supporting framework for a sculpture
questions.explain: An armature is the internal skeleton, often wire, that supports a modelled sculpture.

questions.q: A 'design brief' usually sets out...
options: The client's requirements and the target audience
questions.explain: A design brief defines the task, the client's needs and the intended target audience.

questions.q: What does 'composition' mean in art?
options: The arrangement of elements within an artwork
The size of the canvas only
questions.explain: Composition is how the visual elements are arranged and organised within the picture area.

questions.q: What is 'pattern' as a formal element?
options: A repeated arrangement of shapes, lines or colours
The lightness or darkness of an area
The edge that defines a shape
questions.explain: Pattern is created when elements such as shapes or marks are repeated in an organised way.

questions.q: Which group are considered warm colours?
questions.explain: Reds, oranges and yellows are warm colours, while blues, greens and violets are cool.

questions.q: Which natural fibre comes from the cocoon of the silkworm?
questions.explain: Silk is a natural protein fibre produced by silkworms when they spin their cocoons.

questions.q: What is the secondary colour made by mixing red and yellow?
questions.explain: Red mixed with yellow produces the secondary colour orange.

questions.q: What is 'stippling'?
options: Building tone using many small dots
questions.explain: Stippling builds up tone and texture using numerous small dots placed close together.

questions.q: Abstract Expressionism is characterised by...
questions.explain: Abstract Expressionism used large-scale, energetic, often non-figurative gestural marks.

questions.q: What does adding white to a colour create?
questions.explain: Adding white to a colour produces a tint (a lighter version), while adding black produces a shade.

questions.q: Which printmaking process is described as 'intaglio', where ink is held in lines cut below the surface?
questions.explain: Etching is an intaglio process: ink sits in the recessed bitten lines, not on the raised surface.

questions.q: In a portrait, lighting placed to one side to create strong shadows and modelling is called...
questions.explain: Side lighting rakes across the face, producing shadows that reveal form and texture.

questions.q: 'Surface decoration' in textiles refers to...
options: Patterns or marks added onto the surface of a fabric
The fibre the fabric is made from
The way the cloth is woven
questions.explain: Surface decoration covers techniques such as printing, embroidery or dyeing applied to a fabric's surface.

questions.q: What is 'typography' in graphic design?
options: The art of arranging type and lettering
questions.explain: Typography is the design and arrangement of type so that text is legible and appealing.

questions.q: What is a watercolour 'wash'?
options: Thick paint applied with a knife
A thin, transparent layer of diluted paint
questions.explain: A wash is a thin, transparent layer of watercolour spread over an area to build colour gradually.
